newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chechnya, Russia agree details on fixing pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Chechnya, Russia agree details on fixing pipeline.

text.p: Russia and its rebel region Chechnya have agreed a deal spelling out how they will fix a vital war-damaged pipeline to carry Azeri oil across Chechen territory to the Black Sea, Interfax news agency said on Sunday.
In a report from the Chechen regional capital Grozny, it said the Russian Energy Ministry and Chechnya's YUNKO state oil company signed the detailed agreement late on Saturday.
The pipeline, a key conduit for Azeri oil from Baku on the Caspian Sea to the Russian Black Sea port of Novorossiisk, was damaged during Russia's war with Chechen rebels.

The deal would allow Russian and Chechen companies to "make the necessary contacts and sign agreements to carry out joint work on restoring and using the oil pipeline", Interfax quoted YUNKO president Khodzhakhmed Yarikhanov as saying.
The agency on Saturday quoted Chechen and Russian officials as saying work would begin in the next few days to mend the 153-km (95 mile) section of pipeline, and Moscow would pay.

Saturday's agreement was intended to flesh out a tripartite framework accord signed in the Azeri capital Baku on Friday. Friday's accord was signed by Russian Energy Minister Boris Nemtsov, Yarikhanov and the president of the Azeri state oil company SOCAR.

The deal, held up for months by bickering between the sides over the details, is intended to clear the way for crude output from an $8 billion Western consortium developing off-shore Azeri Caspian Sea fields to reach world markets.
It was not clear how long the work would take, nor when oil would begin to flow. The consortium, led by British Petroleum, wants to begin using the route later this year.

Chechnya has set itself up as a de facto independent entity since the war ended last August. The Kremlin regards Chechnya as one of 89 regions within the Russian Federation, although has adopted a pragmatic approach to several bilateral problems.

Interfax and Itar-Tass news agency said Chechen President Aslan Maskhadov had signed a customs agreement with Russia and met Russian Security Council deputy secretary Boris Berezovsky on Saturday to discuss the pipeline and banking cooperation.
"The signing of these documents is an important step, although there are many more steps ahead," Berezovsky told Interfax.
